info.desc: Vs. is the second studio album by the American alternative rock band Pearl Jam, released on October 19, 1993 through Epic Records. After a relentless touring schedule in support of its debut album, Ten (1991), Pearl Jam headed into the studio in early 1993 facing the challenge of following up the commercial success of its debut. The resulting album, Vs., featured a rawer and more aggressive sound compared with the band's previous release. Pearl Jam decided to scale back its commercial efforts for Vs., including declining to produce music videos for any of the album’s singles. Upon its release, Vs. .

podcast.body: Pearl Jam's highly anticipated album, released in stages in October 1993, features an Angora goat on its cover, not a sheep. The photograph was taken by bassist Jeff Ament at Lifeline Farm in Victor, Montana. The goat, described as friendly and curious, was unaware it was destined for slaughter, a metaphor Jeff Ament used to express the band's feeling of being "slaves to the star making machinery of the popular song," which also explains the original working title, "Five Against One," and the final title, "Vs." Guitarist Stone Gossard stated that the title represented the struggles of making a record and maintaining one's independence and soul "Versus Everyone Else's." Other panels of the album feature symbolic images of human feet walking in mud, representing the band. "The goat, by the way, wasn't angry at all. It was very friendly, very curious and completely oblivious to the fact that it was soon to be slaughtered."

podcast.body: Pearl Jam's highly anticipated follow-up album, released weeks after Nirvana's "In Utero," achieved a stunning opening week with 950,000 copies sold. This set a new record for the largest opening sales in chart history, a record Pearl Jam held for five years. By the end of the 1993 holiday season, it was already quintuple platinum. "Pearl Jam's follow-up opened to a stunning 950,000 copies in its first week, then a record for the largest opening sales in chart history."

podcast.body: Pearl Jam's sophomore album, *Vs.*, released in late 1993, featured major radio hits built around a more rustic, acoustic sound. This shift contributed to a broader trend in alternative rock towards quieter, more upbeat tracks, moving away from the heavier grunge sound. "On Pearl Jam's late 93 sophomore album, Versus, the biggest radio hits were built around a more rustic acoustic sound."

podcast.body: Recorded at an expensive studio called The Site in the San Francisco area at the insistence of Epic Records. Eddie was in his most intense anti-rockstar phase and suffered severe writer's block; he often drove the 30 miles to San Francisco to hang out with homeless people, returning occasionally to work on five or six songs at a time. During the recording of "Rearviewmirror" — the first Pearl Jam song Eddie ever wrote on guitar — drummer Dave Abbruzzese, under intense pressure to get his part right, threw his sticks against the wall at the song's end, punched through the head of his snare drum, marched outside, and threw the snare drum over a cliff. "The tension Eddie felt about this whole rockstar thing spilled over to the rest of the band."

podcast.body: Released on October 19, 1993, Pearl Jam's *Vs.* album achieved remarkable sales figures immediately upon release. Thanks to SoundScan technology, it was precisely known that the album sold 950,378 copies within its first five days. This data solidified the band's status and demonstrated the massive commercial power of alternative rock. "And because of Sound Scan technology, we know that it sold exactly 950,378 copies in the first five days of its release."
